explainers.question: How does boxing scoring actually work?
explainers.answer: Boxing is 10-point must over 12x3 minute rounds where three judges give 10 to the round winner and 9 or 8 to the loser, plus knockdowns cost a point and fouls cost deductions — a close fight is 115-113, a shutout 120-108, and a draw can be split, majority or unanimous.
explain: The 10-point must is the system. The winner of the round gets 10, the loser 9, or 8 if knocked down or dominated, so 12 rounds means 120-108 is a shutout where every round is 10-9, 115-113 is 7-5 with no knockdowns, and a knockdown round is often 10-8 even if the knocked-down fighter won the rest of the round — the knockdown flips the round, not just the punch.

The judges explain the myth. Three judges sit ringside at different angles, each scores every round on clean punching, effective aggressiveness, ring generalship and defence — clean jabs to the head count more than arm punches to the body, and a flurry that lands 3 of 10 counts less than a single straight that snaps the head — which is why the crowd's cheer for volume often disagrees with the judge's card for clean.

A draw is three types. Unanimous decision is 3-0 on cards, split is 2-1, majority is 2-0 with one draw, and a draw itself can be unanimous 114-114, split 115-113/113-115/114-114, or majority 114-114 twice — the 2023 Fury vs Ngannou split shows how one judge's 10-8 for a knockdown can flip a 114-114 to 115-113 and the result with it.

Knockdowns cost a point automatically — a 10-8 without a warning, two knockdowns in one round is 10-7, which is why a fighter who is knocked down in round 1 and wins 11 of 12 can still draw 113-113 if the knockdown was 10-8 and the 11 wins are 10-9 — the knockdown round is worth double a normal round, which is why a single knockdown in a close fight decides more than 5 close rounds.

Fouls add deductions. Low blow, headbutt or holding can cost 1 point after a warning from the referee, announced as 'point deduction for low blow, Judge 1 9-9' — so a 10-9 round becomes 9-9 and the fighter effectively loses the point he would have won, which is why a close fight with two deductions can be 114-114 even with a 7-5 round split.

explainers.question: What are the boxing belts — WBA, WBC, IBF, WBO?
explainers.answer: Boxing belts are 4 sanctioning bodies WBA, WBC, IBF, WBO each with a champion per 17 weight classes, not one belt, with lineal, Ring and undisputed 4-belt vs unified 2-3 belts, mandatories, and the evergreen where Usyk holds 4 heavy and Canelo held 4 at super middle, not one belt as UFC's single belt per weight.
explain: Boxing belts are 4 bodies, 17 weights, 68 champions — WBA (1921 oldest), WBC (1963 green), IBF (1983), WBO (1988) — each weight has WBA regular plus super? Actually WBA has super and regular nonsense — WBA regular plus super per weight gives 5 belts per weight, not 4, which is why heavyweight has Usyk undisputed 4 plus Fury lineal — not lineal belt but Ring magazine's lineal plus 4 sanctioning, so the 4-belt era since 2007 undisputed 4 not 3 as pre-2007 3-belt era.

Undisputed needs 4, unified is 2-3. Undisputed undisputed holds 4 WBA(WBA super), WBC, IBF, WBO at one weight in 4-belt era — Usyk heavy undisputed 2024 after Fury, Crawford at welter 2023, Canelo at super middle 2021 — unified holds 2 of 4 not 4, not undisputed — the WBA regular is not counted for undisputed, so WBA super vs regular's 2 per weight makes regular not — the 4-belt undisputed is the evergreen where 2-belt unification defends vs mandatory WBA's 3.5% purse fee per body vs WBC's 3% with 3% per body means 12% sanction fee for 4 belts, not 3%.

Mandatory vs voluntary explains defence. Each body orders mandatory challenger top 15: WBA 1 is Joshua, WBC 1 Wilder, IBF 1 Parker, WBO 1 Zhang — the 4 bodies each order defence every 9 months, so the undisputed 4 must defend 4 mandatories in 9 months not 12 as UFC's champ may defend 2 of 12 months vs top 15 no mandatory per body — the WBA mandatory 9 months vs WBC 9 vs IBF 9 vs WBO 9 equals unblockable 4 in 9, which is why the 4-belt undisputed typically gets stripped of one for not meeting mandatory WBO's 9 with purse bid 25% challenger not 30% champion's 80% split, not voluntary's 50-50 as UFC's split 45-45 plus show.

The evergreen myth is one belt per weight. Four belts per weight 17 weights 68 champions plus WBA regular's 17 extra plus interim 5 gives 90 belts, not 8 as UFC's 8 men's — heavyweight has Usyk 4 plus Fury lineal Ring, cruiserweight Opetaia IBF plus Ring, so the 4-belt 68 not 8 decides why boxing's 68 champions vs UFC's 8 — each body's $1m fee plus 3% gate means 4% vs UFC's gate 16% to UFC not per body, which is why Canelo's 4-belt undisputed paid 12% sanction 4×3% vs Fury's 1 belt 3% not 12, and why undisputed heavy 4-belt purse bid 80-20 champion vs 45-45 UFC's gate split.

The lineal and Ring plus belts: The Ring belt since 1922 lineal lineage where champion beats champion after vacant via top 2 beating — Fury's lineal via Klitschko 2015 vacated? Actually Fury beat Klitschko 2015 for lineal not belt? Actually lineal heavy Fury from Klitschko then Usyk from Fury 2024 — the Ring's lineal 1 vacancy via top 2 — the 4-belt plus lineal vs Ring is 6 belts per weight not 4, so Usyk lineal plus 4 is the true undisputed 5 not 4, plus IBF regular vs super shows 6.
explainers.example: Heavy 2024: Usyk WBA(WBA super) 3% WBC 3% IBF 3% WBO 3% hold 4 = undisputed heavy 4 plus lineal via Fury 2015 plus Ring — Crawford undisputed welter — 4 bodies 17 weights 68 champions vs UFC 8 — mandatories 9 months per body 4 in 9 not UFC's 2 in 12 — the WBA regular vs super 5 per weight, purse bid 80-20 champion vs challenger 12% sanction fee for 4 belts vs UFC 16% to promo, not per body.

myths.reality: 4 bodies WBA WBC IBF WBO 17 weights 68 champions plus WBA regular 17 — undisputed needs 4, unified is 2-3, not one.
Undisputed is 4 belts WBA WBC IBF WBO since 2007 4-belt era — unified is 2-3, lineal Ring is extra 5th.
Each body's mandatory every 9 months with 3% fee — 4 in 9 months not 2 in 12 as UFC — not voluntary 50-50.

The Clinch 3 seconds vs boxing's break on clinch with referee break — bare clinch 3 secs with punch with one hand plus clinch 3 secs not wrestling — the BKFC's toe line explains start: toe line 3 feet apart as old London Prize Ring's scratch line, not boxing's 10 feet neutral corner's 10 count as 10 sec vs MMA's 8 — the toe line 3 feet plus 3 rounds 2 minutes 10 shows BKFC's 5x2 10 vs bare's 7x2 14 champion 14 vs 36, which is why Perry vs Alvarez 2023 bare 5 rounds x2 10 with toe line 3 feet 10 minutes, not 15 mins 5x5 MMA 25 minutes 5 plus 2 timeouts each OT 5 full 10 vs 5 with 4 team fouls reset to 4 on 5th bonus.

explainers.question: What is MMA — and how does the UFC work?
explainers.answer: MMA is mixed martial arts where a fight can be won by knockout, submission or judges' 10-point must over 3x5 minute rounds (5x5 for titles), and the UFC is the top promotion with weight classes from strawweight to heavyweight, a pound-for-pound ranking, and the champion who holds the belt until beaten or stripped.
explain: MMA blends three bases. Striking from boxing and kickboxing, wrestling for takedowns and control, and jiu-jitsu for submissions — a fighter can win on the feet by knockout at 70% of finishes, on the ground by submission like rear-naked choke at 20%, or on the cards if it goes the distance — which is why a wrestler who controls 10 of 15 minutes on the ground can beat a striker who lands more but is held, and why the style matchup decides more than the record.

The UFC's weight classes are 8 men's and 4 women's, each 10-15 lbs apart — flyweight 125, bantamweight 135, featherweight 145, lightweight 155, welterweight 170, middleweight 185, light heavyweight 205, heavyweight 265 — with a one-pound allowance for non-title fights, so a 170.5 walk-around can make 170, but a 171 cannot without a catchweight, which is why weight cuts of 15-20 lbs in 48 hours are the evergreen health myth.

The rounds explain the scoring. Three rounds 5 minutes for non-title, 5x5 for championship and main events, 10-point must per round — 10-9 for the winner, 10-8 for dominance — but a 10-8 is rarer than boxing because a dominant round with a near-finish is still 10-9 unless the loser is saved by the bell, which is why 29-28 can be 2 rounds to 1 and 30-27 is a shutout, and why a fighter who wins 2 of 3 but is knocked down in the 2nd can still lose 28-28 on that round's 10-8.

Why the UFC dominates is the single promotion. The UFC owns the top 15 per weight class in its ranking, matchmakes champion vs interim, and strips for inactivity — the belt, not a sanctioning body, is the title, so the UFC champion is the world champion in practice, which is why a Bellator or PFL champion who moves to the UFC often enters at 8-10 and must win 2 to challenge, not unify.

The evergreen myth is the cage. The Octagon is 30 feet across with an 8-sided fence, not a ring, so the fence can be used to stand up from a takedown — the wall-walk — and a fighter who grabs the fence loses a point, which is why the cage favours wrestlers who can drive to the fence and strikers who can sprawl, not just boxers who would be trapped in a ring's corner.
explainers.example: July title at lightweight 155: Champion 5x5 vs Challenger 3x5 path — Champion wins rounds 1-2 10-9, Challenger knocks down in round 3 for 10-8, Champion wins 4 10-9, Challenger wins 5 10-9 — 48-46 Champion, 2 rounds lost but the 10-8 third keeps the challenger close, which is why a 3-2 on rounds can be 48-46 not 49-46 — the knockdown round is the swing that boxing also has, but with 5 rounds not 12.

myths.belief: MMA and UFC are the same.
myths.reality: MMA is the sport, UFC is the top promotion — Bellator, PFL and ONE are other promotions where the UFC champion is treated as the world champion.

myths.belief: Any weight can fight any weight.
myths.reality: Eight men's classes 125-265 with 10-15 lbs gaps — a 170 cannot fight at 185 without missing weight and a catchweight, and 265 is the heavyweight cap.
10-point must per 5-minute round, but only 3x5 or 5x5 rounds, so 30-27 is a 3-0 shutout and a 10-8 round is rarer than boxing's.

explainers.question: How does the IPL auction work?
explainers.answer: The IPL auction is the February player draft where 10 franchises bid with ₹120cr ($14.5m) purse for 25 players, with £m bids like Mitchell Starc ₹24.75cr, 4 retained plus auction, 4 foreign max per XI, salary cap 120cr plus uncapped Indians, right-to-match and accelerated after 100+ pool.
explain: The IPL auction is not the draft order with 96 of 1,001 combinations — it is English auction with paddle — base price ₹20 lakh to ₹2cr, increments ₹20 lakh, hammer after 3 calls, with ₹120cr purse per team (about $14.5m), 25 squad max, 18-25 squad size, 4 foreign per XI mandatory, 4 retained October plus 6 via RTM right-to-match now 2025 with 1 RTM, not 5 retain — the 2024 auction had 331 pool, 72 sold, purse left 15cr for unsold not bought.

The retention vs auction explains the myth. Retain 4 max October at ₹16cr-12cr-8cr-6cr =42cr purse spent, the rest ₹78cr for 21 players at auction — the 4 retain leaves ₹78cr to bid vs 0 retain leaves ₹120cr full, which is why KKR retained 4 at 42cr then bought Starc 24.75cr with 78cr left (32% on 1 player), which is why the 4 retain is 42cr flat not per team bid, so CSK retain 2 at 28cr leave 92cr for auction's 7 picks, not 4.

The foreign cap is 8 per squad but 4 per XI — 8 overseas squad max, 4 per XI plus substitute as impact player now — the 4 per XI means CSK's 8th overseas sits while 4 play, which is why Starc 24.75cr Australian pace plays while Hazlewood sits, and why the auction's 331 pool had 77 overseas sold — the 4 per XI not 11 forces the ₹2cr Indian uncapped vs ₹20 lakh base for overseas 1 cr, so value is the 4-per-XI, not the 8 squad.

The hammer decides more than the base — the 2024 auction Starc 24.75cr was 20cr base plus 4.75cr increments of 20 lakh x 24 increments with hammer at 24.75 after Delhi cap 24cr plus KKR 24.75 final — the 24.75 not 25 flat shows the 20 lakh increment from 20cr base to 24.75's 4.75 extra is 24 increments, which is why the auction's accelerated after 100 not sold plus unsold list at 170 players remaining is the TV's 8-hour show with 72 sold, not all 331.

The evergreen is ₹120cr not £. The purse is ₹120cr cap plus salary cap 14.5m USD, the sold 2024 72 cost 230cr total, 72* average 3.2cr vs NBA's 15-man 168m, which is why the IPL's 25 squad at ₹120cr is 4.8cr per 25 vs NBA 15 at $11m per 15, and why the Impact Player now adds 12th per match but not per XI, so the auction's 25 squad for 14 matches with 7 home plus substitutes.

explainers.question: How does LBW work in cricket?
explainers.answer: LBW is leg before wicket — the batter is out if the ball would have hit the stumps but the pad blocked it — with three checks: pitched in line or outside off, impact in line, and hitting the stumps, plus the DRS ball-tracking that overturns the on-field call on umpire's call margins.
explain: LBW is the 10% that confuses. Bowled is hit stumps, caught is hit then caught, lbw is would have hit stumps but pad intervened — the bowler appeals, the umpire judges pitched, impact and hitting, all in 2 seconds, with 0.01 on the edge deciding, which is why lbw is the only dismissal that needs prediction, not just observation, and why the umpire's finger stays down more often than up — 30% of appeals are given lbw, 70% not out.

The three checks decide. Pitched: the ball must have pitched in line between wicket and wicket or outside off — pitched outside leg is never lbw, even if it would have hit, which is why a leg-spinner pitching outside leg and hitting the pad in front of middle is not out. Impact: the pad's first contact must be in line between wicket and wicket, or outside off where the batter was not playing a shot — outside off with a shot offered is not lbw, without a shot it can be, which is why the umpire checks the shot.

Hitting is the third and the myth. The ball must be hitting the stumps — middle and leg, or leg and middle — by more than half the ball, otherwise the tracking shows umpire's call — the on-field call stands if it is nail-biting. That is why the DRS graphic shows red for out, green for not, and yellow for umpire's call — yellow keeps the on-field, red or green overturns, and the width of the yellow is the 50% that creates the controversy.

The DRS review explains the overturn. The batter reviews with the team losing one review per innings if failed, the ball-tracking from 6 cameras predicts the path after the pad, and the third umpire checks pitched, impact and hitting with the ball-tracking — the on-field umpire's soft signal is the base, and the tracking's 2.5mm accuracy decides — the 2023 change to umpire's call on height kept more on-fields, which is why height is now the most common umpire's call, not line.

Why lbw took 100 years is the pad. Before 1935 lbw was rare because batters could kick the ball away outside off with the pad and be not out — Don Bradman averaged 99 that way — then law 36 was changed to allow lbw even with impact outside off if no shot was offered, so the pad could no longer be a second bat — the evergreen law that a batter who pads outside off without offering a shot can be lbw is the 1935 fix, not the original.

Evergreen, the 10% explains the game. LBW is the only dismissal where the batter can be out without the bat or the ball hitting the stumps — the prediction of hitting — which is why the DRS, the umpire's call, and the pitched-outside-leg exception are the cricket equivalent of football's offside frame and line — the 10% that decides 30% of debates.
explainers.example: India vs Australia: Lyon bowls off-spin that pitches outside off, turns, hits the pad in line middle-and-leg with no shot offered, the on-field gives not out, Australia reviews, tracking shows pitched outside off yes, impact in line yes, hitting leg and middle red for out — overturned to out on umpire's call's 50% — the 3-check plus ball-tracking that football's VAR offside line also needs, but with pitched outside leg as the exception that football has no parallel for.

myths.belief: Any pad that blocks the stumps is lbw.
myths.reality: Three checks — pitched in line or outside off, impact in line (or outside off with no shot), and hitting — pitched outside leg is never lbw even if it would have hit.
Yellow is umpire's call — if hitting is 50% on the stumps, the on-field stands — red or green overturns, yellow keeps the finger as it was.

myths.belief: The batter must be playing a shot.
myths.reality: If impact is outside off and no shot is offered, lbw can still be given — the 1935 law to stop pad as a second bat.

faq.a: No — pitched outside leg is never lbw, even if it would have hit — the only pitched exception in the law.

explainers.question: How does cricket ranking work?
explainers.answer: Cricket rankings are 100-point scale updated after each series — Tests, ODIs and T20s each separate, 100 for the best, rating vs ranking plus World Test Championship points 12 per win, not a 52-week roll but a match-by-match gap where Australia over India by 2 points means 2% better.
explain: Cricket rankings are ICC 100-scale per format — Tests, ODIs, T20Is separate with 100 for the top — after each Test or ODI the rating moves about 2 points per match, so India's 120 vs Australia 118 in Tests means India 2% better, not games — the 100 is not 2000 as tennis's 2000, but the 100-scale's 3-point gap can be one Test's 2 points plus one ODI's 1, which is why the ranking moves daily not weekly as tennis's 52-week Monday.

The Test ranking plus WTC contrasts. The ICC Test ranking is 100-scale rating after each Test, but the World Test Championship is table points 12 per win, 4 for draw, 6 for tie, over 2-year cycle 6 series per team, top 2 to Lord's final over 2-year — the ranking is 100 after each Test, the WTC is 0-72 points per cycle, so India can be ranking 1 at 120 but WTC 1 at 58 points and still meet Australia ranking 2 at Lord's.

The evergreen myth is ranking decides qualifiers. The ODI Super League decided 2023 World Cup slots via 10 before, but now ODI ranking 8 plus 2 via qualifier decides — the ranking's 100 decides which 8 auto are in the World Cup 10, not the World Test Championship's 2-year table — the T20 ranking's 100 decides no direct slot but seeds the T20 World Cup's 20 as 12 auto plus 8 via regionals, not ranking's top 20 directly.

Why AfroBasket ranking matters is FIBA vs ICC. The cricket ranking's 100 after each match vs tennis's 52-week expiry vs ATP's 2000 for Slam — the cricket's match-by-move 2 points vs tennis's 52-week drop 2000 at expiration explains why cricket ranking shifts after one T20 upset but tennis's stays for 52 weeks with 0 drop, which is why Nigeria's cricket T20 ranking 40 can jump 6 with 2 wins while ATP's Nj m 40 stays as last year's 360 dropped 52 weeks later, not same week.
explainers.example: ICC 2024: Test ranking India 120, Australia 118 — 2-point gap, WTC Lord's final cycle 12 per win 6 series top 2 vs 100-scale — T20I ranking India 275, Australia 268 — the 100-scale per format vs 2000 men's Slam vs ATP 19, updated per match not Monday — the 8 ODI ranking auto for World Cup 10 plus 2 via qualifier vs WTC 2-year 6 series.

myths.reality: 3 separate 100-scale tables Tests, ODIs, T20Is updated per match, plus WTC 2-year points 12 per win top 2 to Lord's — not one 2000.
ODI ranking 8 auto plus 2 via qualifier for ODIs 10 — the ranking's 8 decides half, not the whole 10.
About 2 per match on 100 scale vs tennis's 2000 for a Slam — the 2-point gap 120 vs 118 is one Test's move.

explainers.question: How does cricket actually work?
explainers.answer: Cricket is 11-a-side where one team bats to score runs by hitting the ball and running between two wickets 20.12m apart, the other bowls to get 10 batters out, and the side with more runs wins — the three formats are Test over 5 days with 90 overs per day, ODI over 50 overs per side in a day, and T20 over 20 overs in 3 hours.
explain: The wicket explains the target. Two stumps with bails at each end 20.12m apart — the bowler bowls from one end to the batter at the other who protects the stumps, and a run is scored when the two batters swap ends after hitting, or 4 if the ball reaches the boundary on the bounce, 6 if it clears on the full. Ten of 11 must be out to end an innings — the not-out batter is stranded, which is why 10 down is all out even with 11.

Bowling explains the defence. The bowler must release with a straight arm, bounce the ball or bowl full, and get the batter out in 10 ways — bowled (hit stumps), lbw (would have hit), caught (hit and caught), run out (stumps hit while running) are the 90% — then the next batter comes in. An over is 6 legal balls, 90 overs per day in Tests, 50 per side in ODIs, 20 in T20s, so a Test innings can be 150 overs over two days while a T20 innings is 20 overs in 85 minutes.

Pitch explains condition. The 22-yard pitch is clay and grass that cracks, so a Day 1 green pitch seams and swings for fast bowlers at 85-90 mph, a Day 4 dry pitch spins for spinners who turn the ball sideways, and a flat pitch does neither — the toss winner often bats if green and bowls if dry, which is why the pitch report before the toss decides the game as much as the players.

Why no draw in white ball is format. Tests can draw after 5 days if time runs out with wickets left — about 20% do — while ODIs and T20s always produce a winner via Super Over if level — one over per side, then second, then boundary count was scrapped after 2019's England vs New Zealand tie where the Super Over also tied and England won on boundaries, now unlimited Super Overs until a winner.

The IPL explains the money. The Indian Premier League is T20 franchise cricket — 10 teams, March-May, $6bn TV deal, players auctioned — where a 20-over innings with 6 sixes and 10 fours can be 200 runs, and a chase of 200 in 20 overs is a par, so the 5-day Test's patience and the 3-hour T20's hitting are the same sport at opposite tempos.
explainers.example: At the 2023 ODI World Cup final in Ahmedabad: Australia bowl first on a dry pitch, India bat and are 240 all out in 50 overs — 240 off 300 balls with 25 fours and 5 sixes — Australia chase 241 off 300 balls in 43 overs with Travis Head scoring 137, 15 fours and 4 sixes, and win by 6 wickets with 7 overs spare — 50 overs per side, 10 down, more runs wins, the ODI format in one scorecard.

myths.reality: Test 5 days 90 overs per day, ODI 50 overs per side in a day, T20 20 overs in 3 hours — same wicket 20.12m apart, three clocks.
10 down is all out — the not-out batter is stranded with no partner, so 10 is the innings end even with 11.
Only Tests can draw on time. ODIs and T20s go to Super Overs until a winner — unlimited since 2019's boundary-count controversy.

faq.a: Test up to 5 days (90 overs per day), ODI about 8 hours (50 overs per side), T20 about 3 hours (20 overs per side).

explainers.question: How does the IPL actually work?
explainers.answer: The IPL is 10 franchises, March-May, 74 games — double round-robin then playoffs — with a March auction for 25-man squads, a ₹120 crore ($14m) purse per team, 4 foreign players max per XI, and a $6bn TV deal that makes it cricket's Premier League where a 6-week tournament pays more than a year of Tests.
explain: The IPL is 10 teams — Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Bangalore, Delhi, Rajasthan, Hyderabad, Punjab, Gujarat, Lucknow — each plays 14 league games home and away, then the top 4 go to playoffs — 1st vs 2nd in Qualifier 1 winner to final, loser to Qualifier 2 vs winner of Eliminator 3rd vs 4th — so the league is 70 games plus 4 playoffs over about 8 weeks, with every game at 19:30 IST for TV, which is why a season has 74 games, not 38 like football.

The auction explains the evergreen question. Squads are 25 — 8 foreign max in squad, 4 per XI — bought at a March auction with a purse of ₹120 crore per team, where the purse left after retentions is the budget, and the lowest base is ₹20 lakh for uncapped. Mitchell Starc went for ₹24.75 crore ($2.9m) in 2024 as the most expensive, while an emerging player goes for ₹20 lakh — the purse, not the wage, is the cap that keeps the league balanced, though retained stars keep a separate pre-auction fee.

Why 4 foreign per XI is the rule is the Indian core. The IPL is the BCCI's domestic league, so 7 of 11 must be Indian, which develops the national team — the same XI that wins the IPL often has 4 Indian bats and 3 Indian bowlers, which is why the IPL is the feeder for India's T20 World Cup squad, not a foreign exhibition, and why an Indian uncapped can become a star in one season.

The TV deal explains the money. The 2023-27 rights were $6.2bn — $1.2bn per year — split 50% to franchises and 50% to the BCCI, so each franchise gets about $50-60m a year before a ball, which is why the purse can be $14m and still profit — the gate is 30,000 at 7:30pm on a weekday, but the TV is 500m viewers, which is the inverse of the football finance that gates first support.

Format vs internationals shows the calendar. The IPL's 8 weeks in March-May clash with England's County, Australia's Sheffield Shield and West Indies' Tests, so boards release their stars for the IPL because the IPL fee for 6 weeks can equal a year's central contract — Jos Buttler's IPL $1m for 14 games vs England's $1.2m for 12 months — which is why the IPL window is now protected and no internationals are scheduled in it.
explainers.example: March auction: Punjab Kings bid ₹24.75 crore for Starc, Gujarat retain Shubman Gill for ₹16 crore pre-auction, then in May Gujarat vs Mumbai at Narendra Modi Stadium with 100,000 — Mumbai post 218 in 20 overs with 12 sixes, Gujarat chase 219 with Gill 104 off 55, win by 3 wickets — 74 games later the final is in Chennai with 2.5 crore viewers per ball, the IPL's 8-week 74-game sprint that pays more than a 5-day Test series.

explainers.question: What are the Ashes — and how do they work?
explainers.answer: The Ashes is the 5-Test, 25-day Test series between England and Australia played every 2 years over 7 weeks, alternating hosts — 5 Tests of up to 5 days each, 15 sessions per Test, winner keeps the tiny urn said to hold burnt bail from 1882, drawn retains, with no DRS needed in 1882 but now every ball.
explain: The Ashes is 5 Tests over 7 weeks — Test 1 late November in Brisbane or June in Edgbaston, Test 5 early January in Sydney or late July at The Oval — 5 days per Test, 6 hours per day (2 sessions morning-afternoon-evening plus lunch and tea), 15 sessions per Test, 75 sessions for the Ashes, winner 2-2-3? The series winner gets the urn, drawn 2-2 retains to the holder — Australia retained 2-2 in 2023 at The Oval, England needed 3-2 to win, which is why the 2-2 Ashes stays with the holder, not the challenger.

The urn is the myth. The tiny 10cm tall urn at Lord's says the ashes of English cricket burnt and now at Lord's — the 1882 Sporting Times mock obituary after England's loss at The Oval to Australia — the replica goes to the winner, the original stays in the MCC museum, so Stokes and Cummins lift the replica Crystal, not the 1882 clay, which is why the Ashes photo is the replica, not the museum piece.

The sessions explain the war. Five days times 3 sessions — 12.00-13.00 morning, 13.40-15.40 afternoon, 16.00-18.00 evening in England, plus 30 overs per session — the 2023 Ashes second Test at Lord's had 32 wickets in 3 days of swing, which is why the Ashes is not 5 ODIs but 5 five-day campaigns where the Dukes ball swings day 1 and Kookaburra day 2, not white ball with floodlights and 50 overs.

The law twist is Bodyline. The 1932-33 Ashes had England's Bodyline short-pitched at the body to Bradman — the bouncer's fast leg theory — the law changed to 2 bouncers per over, now 2 — the Ashes' 2 is the evergreen law that 2 bouncers over shoulder per over is legal, third is no ball, which is why the fast 90 mph Jofra Archer bouncer in 2019 that hit Smith still counts as one of two, not a foul, and why the Ashes' bouncer count is the umpire's finger, not football's card.

The evergreen is 1882. The Ashes is the oldest trophy in sport contested since 1883 after the 1882 obituary — the only urn where drawn retains — the 2019 series 2-2 Australia retained after 2-2, 2021-22 4-0 Australia at home, which is why the away Ashes is the hardest in sport: Australia has not won in England since 2001, England has not won in Australia since 2010-11, the 7-week 5-Test removes the one-game upset.
explainers.example: 2023 Ashes: England vs Australia — 5 Tests: Edgbaston Australia win by 2 wickets, Lord's Australia by 43 runs, Headingley England by 3 wickets, Old Trafford draw rain, The Oval England win — 2-2, Australia retained the urn's replica — 25 days over 7 weeks, 75 sessions, 5 days per Test, Bodyline's 2 bouncers still the law, urn 10cm at Lord's, drawn retains the 1882 ashes.

myths.reality: 5 Tests of 5 days over 7 weeks — 75 sessions, drawn 2-2 retains to holder, so the away team needs 3-2 not 2-2.
Replica only — original 10cm at Lord's museum since 1882 obituary, replica is the photo with Stokes or Cummins.
2 per over over shoulder — third is no ball — the Bodyline 1932-33 law still governs the 90 mph Archer bouncer.

faq.q: How many Tests in the Ashes?
faq.a: 5 Tests of 5 days over 7 weeks, 15 sessions per Test — holder retains on 2-2 draw.
10cm urn at Lord's since 1882 Sporting Times obituary — replica goes to series winner.
1932-33 leg-theory bouncers at the body — law now 2 bouncers per over over shoulder, third is no ball.

explainers.question: What are Test, ODI and T20 in cricket?
explainers.answer: Test is the 5-day, 450-over chess with red ball and white clothes where results can be wins or draws; ODI is the 50-over, 300-ball day game with white ball and coloured shirts where 280 is par; T20 is the 20-over, 120-ball sprint where 170 is par — the same 22-yard pitch, three clocks, three tactics.
explain: Test is 5 days, two innings per side, no over limit per innings — a team can bat 150 overs over two days to make 450, then bowl 90 overs a day to take 20 wickets — the red ball swings more under clouds, the white clothes and lunch and tea breaks pace the day, and the draw exists because time can run out with wickets left, which makes declaration — the captain ending his own innings early to have time to bowl — the Test's unique risk, as when Ben Stokes declares at 250 for a chase.

ODI is 50 overs per side, one innings each in a day — 300 balls, white ball, black sightscreens, coloured shirts, powerplays where only 2-5 fielders are outside the 30-yard circle, so 50 overs has 3 powerplays — 0-10 with 2 outside, 11-40 with 4, 41-50 with 5 — which shapes the tempo: 0-10 hit over the top, 11-40 rotate, 41-50 slog with 6 sixes, where 280-320 is the evergreen par score that 50 overs can produce.

T20 is 20 overs per side, 120 balls, about 85 minutes per innings — the powerplay is 6 overs with 2 outside, then 14 with 5, so the tempo is 6-4-6 — hit 50 in the first 6, rotate 60 in the middle 8, hit 60 in the last 6, where 170 is par, 200 is match-winning and 150 is defendable only with 3 wickets in the powerplay, which is why T20 teams pick 6-7 batters and 4-5 bowlers, not 5 and 5 like Tests.

Why the ball changes is visibility. Test red ball for day, pink for day-night Tests, white for ODIs and T20s under lights — the white swings less than red but is seen under floodlights, so the 50-over and 20-over games are white-ball, day-night or night, while Tests are red-ball day or pink day-night, which is why a pink-ball Test swings at twilight more than a red-ball day test.

The IPL is T20 only, The Hundred is 100 balls per side, not 120, with 10 balls per bowler — the English invention to shorten T20 by 20 balls — and The Ashes is Tests only, 5 Tests over 6 weeks, which is why the format, not the opponent, decides whether a player is a Test specialist like Anderson or a T20 specialist like Russell who barely plays Tests.

Evergreen, the formats select different players. Test picks the batter who can leave the ball for 5 hours and the bowler who can swing the red for 20 overs a day, ODI picks the 360-degree hitter who can rotate and slog, T20 picks the 110mph fast bowler and the 6-hitting finisher who can win in 20 balls — three formats, three squads, one 22-yard pitch.
explainers.example: June Test at Lord's: England bat first, make 450 over 150 overs in two days with Root 150, then Australia bat 500 over 170 overs, England bat again 200 over 60 overs, set Australia 150 to win on Day 5, Australia chase 150 in 40 overs with 8 wickets left — 5 days, 450 overs, two innings each, draw possible — while the same two teams at the T20 World Cup play 20 overs each in 3 hours for 180 vs 170 — same rivalry, 150 overs vs 40, draw vs no draw.

myths.reality: Test 5 days 450 overs, ODI 50 overs in a day, T20 20 overs in 3 hours — three clocks on the same 22-yard pitch.

myths.belief: ODI and T20 are the same.
myths.reality: ODI 50 overs has 3 powerplays and 280 par, T20 20 overs has 1 powerplay and 170 par — the 30 fewer overs change the batting, not just the time.
Tests can draw after 5 days if time runs out — about 20% do — while ODIs and T20s always produce a winner via Super Over.

explainers.question: What are cricket fielding positions?
explainers.answer: Cricket has 11 fielders in named positions around the 30-yard circle: slip, gully, point, cover, mid-off, mid-on, square leg, fine leg, third man, with 2 inside the circle mandatory in powerplay, not 9 in baseball, with long-on and deep mid-wicket 70m from the bat for the 6.
explain: The circle plus boundary explain the set. The 11 fielders have 2 wicketkeeper and bowler plus 9 — slips behind keeper for edges, gully square for cuts, point for cuts, cover for drives, mid-off/on for straight, mid-wicket for pulls, square leg for sweeps, fine leg behind legs, third man behind keeper — the long-on and long-off 70m on the boundary for the 6, not the infield's slip/gully 5m — the 9 can be set as 2 slips + gully vs new ball, then 1 slip + cover vs spin.

The powerplay shifts the set. Powerplay 1-10 2 outside means 7 inside — slips 1, point 1, cover 1, mid-off 1, mid-on 1, square leg 1, keeper 1 — not long-on 70m — the death 41-50 with 5 outside means long-on, long-off, deep mid-wicket, deep cover, third man 5 on the rope for the 6, which is why the ODIs 320 sets the field: powerplay 1-10 with long-on hidden 7 inside, death with 5 long on the rope.

The slip cordon explains the new ball. First 10 overs with Dukes swing have 3 slips and gully 4 behind the bat for edges at 85 mph — the slip 1m from keeper, gully 5m — the cordon catches 30% of wickets in the powerplay vs 10% after, which is why the Ashes' first 10 overs have 3 slips and the IPL's white ball with no swing after 2 overs has 1 slip, not 3, and why the 3-slip cordon is the Ashes' 15-session, not ODI's 10-over, set.

The leg trap is the myth. Fine leg deep behind square vs sweep, square leg for the pull, short leg under the helmet for bat-pad vs spin — the 11 cannot be 6 on leg before the ball (2 behind square max), which is why the leg trap's 5 on leg is fine leg + short leg + square leg + mid-wicket + mid-on, not 6 behind square — the law caps 2 behind square on leg, so the field's 11 is not open like baseball's 9.

The evergreen is off vs leg. Off side is where the bat faces, leg is behind — the field is set off-heavy vs right-hander with 7 on off, leg with 4, vs switch-hit the off retains — the Ashes' right-arm over to right-hander's off is the 3-slip cordon off, not leg, which is why the off's cover 20m and point 25m are the drive's catchers, not the leg's sweep.
explainers.example: ODI powerplay 1-10: 2 outside so slips 1, gully 1, point 1, cover 1, mid-off/on, square leg — death 41-50: 5 outside long-on 70m, long-off, deep mid-wicket, deep cover, third man — Ashes new ball 3 slips plus gully 4 behind for Dukes swing vs IPL white after 2 overs 1 slip — the 11's 9 minus keeper/bowler set as off vs leg, not 9 infield as baseball's 9.

myths.reality: 11 fielders named slip, gully, point, cover, mid-off/on, square leg, fine leg, third man — 2 slips plus gully vs new ball, 5 long on rope death.
Powerplay 1-10 2 outside =7 inside — 3 slips not long-on 70m — death 5 outside =5 long on rope for the 6.
Max 2 behind square on leg — short leg + fine leg behind square capped, so 5 on leg not 6.

concepts.note: the 3 slips the Dukes ball needs

faq.a: 11 — 9 plus keeper and bowler — slip, gully, point, cover, mid-off/on, square leg, fine leg, third man, long-on 70m.
3 slips behind keeper for edges vs new ball swing — 30% of wickets powerplay, 1 slip later vs spin.
Max 2 behind square on leg — fine leg + short leg capped, so 5 on leg total, not 6.

explainers.question: What is ODI powerplay vs middle overs?
explainers.answer: ODI middle overs 11-40 are 30 overs with 4 fielders outside the circle, not 5 as death 41-50, so middle's 30 builds 135 at 4.5 per over with rotation not slog, vs powerplay 60 at 6 and death 125 at 12.5, which is why middle's 30 is the control with 4 outside, not power.
explain: Middle overs 11-40 are 30 overs with 4 outside — 60% of innings with 4 outside, not 2 as powerplay 1-10 — the 4 outside means cover, mid-off, mid-on, square leg inside + point + fine leg? Actually 4 outside means 5 inside mandatory with 2 catchers? The middle's 4 outside with 5 inside plus keeper/bowler makes 7 inside, not 9 as death's 5 outside with 6 inside — the 7 inside lets the single to long-on 2 runs, not 1, so middle's 30 goes at 4.5 per over with 30 singles plus 2 fours per over, not powerplay's 6 per over with 3 fours.

Why middle matters is rotation. The 30 middle's 135 at 4.5 requires 80 singles + 10 fours + 2 sixes =135 off 180 balls, so 80 singles 44% is the rotation with 4 outside's gaps vs death's 5 outside's ropes where 6s force long-on 70m not single gap — the middle's 4 outside's gap at cover 45m vs long-on 70m is 25m extra gap, which is why Root's 50 in the middle 11-40 with 30 singles plus 4 fours is 4.5 not slog's 8.

The evergreen myth is 50 overs flat. Powerplay 10 with 2 outside 60, middle 30 with 4 outside 135 death 10 with 5 outside 125 =320 par, so powerplay 19% of innings has 19% of runs 60 vs 18.75%? Actually middle 42%, death 39% — the 30 middle is 42% runs with 60% overs, so per over 4.5 vs 6 and 12.5, which is why the 300 chase needs 60 in powerplay plus 135 middle plus 125 death, not 100 each 10 = 6 per over flat — the shape's 6 plus 4.5 plus 12.5 is the evergreen that run-rate's 6 flat misses.

The captain's field for middle vs powerplay 1-10 with 2 outside — powerplay 1-10 2 outside has slips 1 plus gully vs middle's 11-40 4 outside has no slip, point + cover + mid-off/on + square leg with 4 on rope? Actually middle's 4 outside means long-on not in 1-10, so middle's long-on 70m saves the 4, powerplay's long-on hides inside for the 4 over top — the middle's no-slip vs powerplay's slip 1 shows the ball's old swing vs middle's no swing, which is why the 3-slip cordon hides after 10 with 4 outside.

The death's 41-50 with 5 outside 125 at 12.5 per over with long-on 70m saves but batter clears — the 5 outside means long-on 70m, long-off, deep cover, deep mid-wicket, third man 5 on rope for the 6 vs middle's 30 with 4 outside's long-on 70m maybe not? Actually death's 5 outside 5 ropes vs middle's 4 outside 4 ropes — the one rope is the difference 1 per over 7 vs 8per over, not 2 as powerplay's 2 outside's 7 inside vs 5 outside's 6 inside, which is why middle's 4.5 vs death's 12.5 is 8 per over gap.
explainers.example: ODI: powerplay 1-10 2 outside 60 at 6 per over, middle 11-40 30 with 4 outside 135 at 4.5, death 41-50 10 with 5 outside 125 at 12.5 — 320 par with 6 +4.5 +12.5, not 6 flat — the middle's 80 singles plus 10 fours 2 sixes =135, powerplay's 3 fours per over 60 vs middle's 30 singles plus fours at cover 45m gap vs death's long-on 70m.

myths.reality: Powerplay 10 with 2 outside 60 at 6, middle 30 with 4 outside 135 at 4.5, death 10 with 5 outside 125 at 12.5 — 320 par shaped, not flat 6.
Middle 11-40 4 outside 7 inside not 5 outside 6 inside — one rope less than death, so single to long-on 2 runs gap 25m extra vs long-on 70m.
Middle's 30 with 4 outside rotation 80 singles 44% plus 10 fours 2 sixes =135 at 4.5 — Root's 50 is singles plus 4, not slog.

concepts.note: the 10 with 2 vs 30 with 4 vs 10 with 5

faq.q: What is middle overs in ODI?
faq.a: 11-40 30 overs with 4 outside the 30-yard circle, 135 at 4.5 per over — 60% of innings 42% of runs.

faq.q: Why powerplay vs middle vs death differ?
faq.a: Powerplay 10 with 2 outside 60 at 6, middle 30 with 4 outside 135 at 4.5, death 10 with 5 outside 125 at 12.5 — 320 par shape, not 6 flat.
No slip after 10 — cover + point plus 4 outside's long-on 70m vs powerplay's 3 slips plus gully vs new ball.

explainers.question: What is Duckworth-Lewis in cricket?
explainers.answer: Duckworth-Lewis-Stern is the rain rule that resets the target by overs and wickets lost, not just overs — the resource is overs x wickets, so 50 overs with 10 wickets is 100% resource, 20 overs with 8 left is 68%, and the target is par plus one, used in 2023 World Cup 4 games, not just a run-rate.
explain: DLS is resource, not rate. overs x wickets is resource — 50 overs 10 wickets 100%, 20 overs 10 wickets 52% by table, 20 overs with 8 left 48% — the table's resource % decides the par score for the chaser, so a chase of 300 in 50 needs 60 per 10 not 6 per over flat — the wickets in hand add resource, which is why 100-2 in 20 needs more than 100-5 in 20, not the same as run-rate's 5 per over.

The calculation steps explain the myth. Team 1 300 in 50 overs 100% — rain cuts chase to 30 overs for Team 2, Team 2 resource 59% (30 overs 10 wickets) — target = 300 * 59/100 = 177 plus 1 = 178 to win if no wickets lost at cut — if Team 2 was 100-2 in 20 at cut, resource used 32% plus remaining 18 overs 4 wickets 42% = 74% resource, so target = 300*74/100=222, not 178 — the wickets before cut shift the par that run-rate would miss by 44 runs.

The Stern revision added modern scoring. Since 2014 the DLS includes 200+ scores in ODIs, so the par for 350 is not 300*0.59 but 350's resource adjusted for high-scoring, which is why the 2023 World Cup's 4 rain games at DLS had targets 340 par plus 1, not 300 — the Stern raised high-score DLS by 3% vs high-rate, which is why the par 150 in T20 under DLS is not 250*0.5 but 250's table at 20 overs 57%.

The evergreen bottleneck is 20 overs needed. DLS needs 20 overs minimum in ODI for a result, 5 in T20 — under 20 overs ballsed, no result if rain before 20, so the 18-over chase that rain stops at 18-3 is no result, not DLS at 18 — the 20 is the threshold that 2019 and 2023 World Cup both have as the DLS cut line, which is why the TV shows DLS par plus 1 only after 20.

The T20 DLS is similar with 20 as 100% resource — 10 overs 10 wickets is 63% resource, not 50%, so 180 chase in 10 overs is 180*0.63/100 = 114 plus 1 =115, not 90 — the overs x wickets resource table's curve is concave, not linear, which is why 10 overs needs 63% not 50% — the curve is the table's heart that run-rate's linear 9 per over misses.

explainers.question: What is the powerplay in cricket?
explainers.answer: The powerplay is the fielding restriction of overs 1-10 with 2 fielders outside the 30-yard circle, overs 11-40 with 4 outside, overs 41-50 with 5 outside — the 10-30-10 split in ODI that decides 320 par, not the batting team's choice, with T20's 6 overs powerplay 2 outside then 14 with 5.
explain: The ODI powerplay is 10-30-10. Overs 1-10 2 fielders outside circle, 11-40 4 outside, 41-50 5 outside, plus 2 fielders in catching positions in 1-10 — the 10 with 2 outside forces the openers to hit over the top for 4s inside, which is why the powerplay 1-10 goes at 60 per 10 vs middle 40-45 per 10, but middle's 30 with 4 outside is the build, not slog — the 10-30-10 decides the 50's shape: powerplay 60, middle 135, death 125 =320 par.

The T20 powerplay is 6 overs with 2 outside, 14 with 5 outside. The T20 20 overs split 6 with 2 outside then 14 with 5 — the 6 is 50-55 vs 170 par, so the powerplay is 30% of innings, not 20% as ODI's 10 is 20% — the 6 with 2 makes the T20 opeler's 30 off 18 more valuable than ODI's 30 off 30, which is why the IPL's 6-over 55 sets the 170, not the ODI's 10-over 60, and why the 6's 2-outside is the 10's twin with 20% less time.

The batting choice powerplay is old ODI before 2015 — the batting powerplay 5 overs with 3 outside was chosen by batting side overs 11-40, removed 2015 to fix the 10-30-10 mandatory, which is why the 2023 World Cup's powerplay's 10-30-10 is not chosen — the 2011 World Cup had batting and bowling powerplays, the 2015 law replaced with 10-30-10 default.

The field circle matters. The 30-yard circle is 30 yards from stumps, within which 4 fielders must be in powerplay 1, 2 catchers in that 4 — the 4 inside the circle is the bottleneck that 2 outside leaves 7 inside including keeper and bowler, so the 2-outside powerplay is 7 inside, not 9 as 5 outside later, which is why the powerplay's 2 allows the loopy 4 over mid-off, not the flat 6 over extra cover vs 5 outside.

The evergreen myth is powerplay is batting choice. Since 2015 it is fixed 10-30-10 — the captain not the batter decides no choice, which is why the powerplay's 10-30-10 shape is 60 + 135 +125 =320, not the batter's 5-over choice, and why T20's 6 plus 5-outside 14 is also fixed, not optional, like football's 15-min halftime fixed, not the captain's.

myths.reality: Fixed 10-30-10 ODI — 1-10 2 outside, 11-40 4 outside, 41-50 5 outside — not chosen since 2015, and T20's 6 plus 14 is also fixed.
10 of 50 =20% ODI, but 6 of 20 =30% T20 — so T20 powerplay 55 in 6 sets 170, ODI's 60 in 10 plus middle 135 death 125 sets 320.

explainers.question: What is the Cricket World Cup?
explainers.answer: The ODI Cricket World Cup is 10 teams over 47 days every 4 years — 10 play a single round-robin 9 games each, top 4 to semis, single elimination to the final over 100 overs per day, not 20, with the 2023 India 10-0 group then 12-man heartbreak the evergreen.
explain: The ODI World Cup is 10 teams in 2023 and 2027 — 10 play single round-robin 9 each over 45 days, then 1st vs 4th and 2nd vs 3rd semis single game over 100 overs (50 per side), final over 100 overs at Ahmedabad's 132,000 — the 10 not 32 makes the 9-group the league, not the group, which is why Afghanistan's 4 wins in 2023 still meant 6th and out, while 4 in football's 3-group can mean knockout — the 9 vs 3 defines the footprint.

The qualifier explains India 2023's depth. The World Cup Qualifier with 10 teams for the last 2 spots — 2 of 32 Associates plus Full Members — Sri Lanka and Netherlands qualified via Zimbabwe 2023 for the 10, so the 10 are 8 auto plus 2 via qualifier, which is why West Indies missed the 2023 World Cup for the first time — the 10, not 14 as in 2015, needs 2 via qualifier, not just ranking, so the 2015 14-team left no qualifier bottleneck but the 10-team did.

The 50 overs explains the day. One innings 50 overs of 6 balls — 300 balls per innings, 600 per day, 8 hours including lunch, with powerplay 10 overs with 2 fielders outside circle, 30 overs with 4 outside, 10 with 5 outside — the powerplay's 10-30-10 sets the field that decides 320 par, not the 200 of T20's 20 overs, which is why the ODI 400 is rare and 320 is par, not 170 as in T20 or 450 as in Test's 90 overs per day.

The evergreen is 2019 tie. England vs New Zealand tie 241-241 in the final, super over tie 15-15, boundary countback gave England the win on 26-17 — the law since changed to successive super overs until win, no countback — the 2019 26-17 boundary is the only World Cup won on boundaries, not runs, which is why the ODI laws now have two super overs, not one plus boundaries, like football's away goals now removed.

The T20 World Cup is 20 teams now 2024 — 20 teams, 4 groups of 5, top 2 to Super 8, then semis — the ODI is 10 over 47 days, T20 20 over 29 days, so the ODI's single round-robin 9 is the endurance league, T20's 5-group is the sprint, which is why the IPL's 74 games feed the T20 World Cup more than the ODI — the 50 vs 20 splits the preparation.

Super over — 2019 tie 241-241 plus super 15-15 was England on 26-17 boundaries, now successive super overs, not countback.

explainers.question: What is the T20 World Cup?
explainers.answer: The T20 World Cup is 20 teams every 2 years over 28 days — 20 play 4 groups of 5, top 2 to Super 8, top 4 to semis, single 20-over 3-hour games, winner plays 9 games not 50 overs, with the 2026 India defence the 20-team 9-game path that the ODIs 10-team 9-game mirrors in time not overs.
explain: The T20 World Cup is 20 since 2024 expanded from 16 — 4 groups of 5 over 12 days, top 2 per group to Super 8, Super 8 as 2 groups of 4, top 2 per to semis single knockout — the 20's 4x5 means 4 group games per team, not 9 as ODI's 10 single round-robin, which is why Uganda and USA made 2024 as the 20's Associates 8 of 20, while ODI's 10 has 0 Associates via qualifier except Netherlands — the 20 gives 8 Associate spots, the 10 gives 2.

The Super 8 explains the stage. After 4x5, the 8 carry over seeding not points — 8 to 2 groups of 4 play 3 each, top 2 to semis — the Super 8 is 3 games not 4, so the 2024 Super 8 Group 1 had India, Australia, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, each 3 — the 8's 3 decides the semi with one surprise (Afghanistan over Australia), which is why the T20 World Cup's Super 8 is the ODI's top 4 semis' twin with 8 not 4, longer but still single KO after.

The 20-over shapes the 3 hours. Twenty overs per side, 120 balls per innings, 6 overs powerplay 2 outside then 14 with 5, innings 90 minutes plus 20 interval, game 3:30, not ODI's 8 hours or Test's 30 hours — the T20's 120 balls par 170 means 8 per over vs ODI's 320 at 6.4 per over, which is why the T20's 6 vs 14 powerplay's 55 in 6 is 30% of innings, not 20% as ODI's 10, and why IPL's 74 games in 20 overs feeds the T20 World Cup's 20-over, not 50.

The evergreen is 2024 co-host. USA and West Indies co-host 2024 with USA beating Pakistan in group, which is why the 20's co-host's 2 games at 6am India prime-time matter as the 20's gate for Associates — the associate 8 of 20 got Dallas's 6am game because India's prime was Dallas midnight, which is why the 20's Dallas 2024 surface issue was the 6am start for India, not for Dallas, like AFCON's 14:00 for Europe vs 17:00 for Africa.

The qualifier feeds the 20. The 20 qualify via regionals: Europe 2, Africa 2, Americas 1, Asia 3, plus auto 12 — the 12 auto plus 8 via regionals means Kenya can qualify via Africa 2 as 2-1 over Zimbabwe, not ranking alone — the 20's 12 auto is Super 8 plus host, not just ranking, which is why 2026 hosts India and Sri Lanka auto plus 2024 Super 8 eight plus 10 via regionals =20.

explainers.question: Why do cricketers wear white and use a red ball in Tests?
explainers.answer: Cricket white and red ball is the Test's noon-to-evening 5-day daylight game under no floodlights — white clothes for sight of the red ball, not fashion — red Dukes or Kookaburra with lacquer that swings day 1, 90 overs per day, 2 new balls after 80 overs, vs white ball in ODIs/T20 under lights 50/20 overs where sight is white ball on green not red.
explain: The Test's white explains the ball. White clothes at 2pm sun show the red ball's seam vs crowd's white sight screen — the red's lacquer shines day 1 with 425g cork and 4-piece leather seam that swings 1.5m at 85 mph with handmade seam — the Duke's hand-stitched seam proud vs Kookaburra machine seam flat decides swing 1st day not 5th — the white's 4.75oz plus red's 5.5oz? Actually red's 163g, white 163g same but lacquer red vs white — the white clothes show red, not hide, like tennis's white vs yellow ball at SW19's green?

The red ball's 80-over two. After 80 overs or 280 runs the fielding captain can take new ball — shiny lacquered side swings more than rough 80-over old with 20 overs reverse — the new ball's seam 80 overs with lacquer shiny then 80-overs old with reverse at 30° seam after scuff, which is why Anderson's 700 wickets are 80-over new with swing plus 80-overs old reverse, not white ball's 1 innings 50 with white lacquer that never reverse after 50 overs with 2 balls 25 each.

The white ball's 2 balls per innings ODI explains why ODIs are day-night under floodlights — the white ball's lacquer with white clothes under lights shows the 6, not red under sun — the white ball is used for 50 overs ODIs and 20 T20 with 2 balls 34 overs each (one from each end) after 2011, which is why DRS's ball tracking for LBW shows white vs red with seam 2.6mm vs 3mm, and why the IPL's white ball with black seam at 20:00 floodlight vs Test's red at 14:00 sun decides no DRS need for white ball's 50 but need for red's 90 per day.

The floodlight's myth is Test under lights pink ball. The day-night Test pink ball vs red at 14:00 with lights at 18:00 — pink ball for evening 14:00-21:00 Test, not red under lights as red is invisible under floodlight's green — the pink's 163g same but lacquer pink with black seam for 30 overs then pink faded, which is why the Ashes day-night Test at Adelaide 17:00 pink swings under lights more than red at 14:00 sun, like hard's roof vs clay's open.

The evergreen is 90 overs per day vs 600 per day ODI's 8 hours vs T20's 240 per 3:30 — the white's 90 overs 11:00-13:00 lunch 13:40-15:40 tea 16:00-18:00 with 6 overs per hour 3 overs per umpire plus drinks — the white clothes plus red ball plus 90 overs 6 hours plus tea plus 2 new balls 80 overs shape the Ashes' 5 Tests 7 weeks 75 sessions vs ODIs 10-team 47 days vs T20 20-team 29 days.

explainers.question: What is the Tour de France?
explainers.answer: The Tour de France is cycling's 21-stage, 3-week Grand Tour over about 3,400km in July — 8 riders per team, 22 teams, yellow for the overall leader by time, green for sprint points, polka dot for mountain points, white for best young, with the winner decided by total time, not stage wins.
explain: The Tour is 21 stages over 23 days with two rest days, about 3,400km — 7 flat stages for sprinters at 50 km/h, 6 mountain stages in the Pyrenees and Alps with 2,000m climbs like Alpe d'Huez, 6 hilly medium, and 2 time trials where each rider races alone against the clock. The yellow jersey is the lowest total time — not most wins — so a rider who wins no stage can win the Tour if he is 2nd on every mountain, which happened in 1968.

The jerseys explain the parallel races. Yellow is overall time, green is sprint points at intermediate sprints and stage finishes, polka dot is mountain points at summits by category — hors catégorie highest — white is best under-26 by time, so one stage has four competitions: the break takes the polka, the sprinter takes green, the GC favourite protects yellow, the young rider attacks for white, all in the same 180km road.

The team explains the win. Twenty-two teams of 8 — 18 WorldTour plus 4 wildcard — ride as a train: domestiques fetch bottles, set tempo on the climb at 20 km/h to drop rivals, and the leader sits in the wheels at 30% less wind until the last 2km, so the Tour winner is the strongest who also has the strongest team — the leader's 7 helpers can be the difference between keeping yellow by 8 seconds or losing it on the Ventoux.

Time gaps decide more than stages. A flat stage win is often 0 seconds gap — the bunch finishes with the same time — while a mountain stage can create 2 minutes — the GC is won in the 3 mountain stages where gaps open, not the 7 flats where the bunch finishes together, which is why a sprinter can win 5 stages and be 100th overall, and a GC rider like Pogacar can win the Tour with 3 stage wins.

The evergreen myth is doping. The Tour's EPO era 1990s-2006 saw 7 Armstrong titles stripped, so the post-2010 Tour added the biological passport, where blood values are tracked longitudinally and a 2% reticulocyte swing triggers a target test — the 21-stage 3,400km is now the most tested event in sport, which is why the 2020-24 winners are seen as the clean generation, not the 2000s'.

Women's explains the gap. La Tour Femmes is 8 stages over 8 days in July after the men's, not 21 — the women's Yellow also by time, but over 950km, which started in 2022 after the old 14-stage version folded, so the men's Tour's 21-stage 3,400km remains the longest Grand Tour vs the Giro and Vuelta at 21 stages but about 3,200km.
explainers.example: July: Stage 17 to Courchevel — 165km, 5,000m climbing, break goes at km 10, polka leader takes 20 points on the Madeleine, Pogacar attacks on the last 7km at 20 km/h, gains 45 seconds on Vingegaard, yellow changes shoulders by 8 seconds, green sprinter finishes 25 minutes down but keeps green, 8 riders per team, 22 teams, yellow by total time, not the stage win.

explainers.question: How does golf actually work — and what are the four majors?
explainers.answer: Golf is 18 holes, lowest strokes wins, with the four majors — Masters at Augusta in April, PGA Championship in May, US Open in June, The Open at links in July — each 156 players over 4 rounds of 18 holes, 72 holes total, cut after 36 holes to top 65 and ties, and the winner gets the green jacket, Wanamaker, or Claret Jug.
explain: The 18 holes explain par. Each hole has par 3, 4 or 5 — par 4 is 380-450 yards to the hole in 2 shots plus 2 putts, par 5 is 530+ with 3 shots, par 3 is 180-220 in 1 shot — the course par is 70-72 over 18 holes, so 4 rounds par is 280-288, and the winner is the lowest over 72 holes, not the most holes won, which is why a 65 in round 1 and a 75 in round 4 can still be 280 total.

The four majors are separate owners. The Masters is Augusta National's invitational 88-90 players based on past champions and world ranking, the PGA is the PGA of America's 156, the US Open is the USGA's 156 with qualifying, The Open is the R&A's 156 links — the majors share no tour, so a LIV player like Koepka can play the majors via the qualifiers but not the regular PGA Tour's FedEx events, which is why the majors are the only place LIV and PGA meet.

The cut explains the weekend. After 36 holes (two rounds) the field cuts to top 65 and ties — about half go home Friday night — so the weekend is 70-85 players over 36 holes, with the leader teeing last on Sunday at about 14:30 local. The cut at 4 over can keep a 3-time major winner in while a world number 5 on 5 over goes home, which is why the Thursday-Friday grind is survival, not just score.

Why links matters is wind. The Open at St Andrews or Royal Liverpool is links — firm, treeless, wind 15-25 mph — so the ball bounces 40 yards and pot bunkers trap, while the Masters at Augusta is parkland with soft greens that stop, so the same 7-iron is 150 yards at Augusta with spin and 130 at St Andrews with wind, which is why a Masters winner often misses the Open cut and the Open winner often misses the Masters cut.

The evergreen bottleneck is 72 holes. A 3-shot lead with 6 holes left is about 70% to win, but the 18th at Augusta or the 17th at Sawgrass can flip it — a double bogey 6 on a par 4 moves -10 to -8 and the chaser's 66 from -8 to -10 wins, which is why final-round 65s like Nick Faldo's 65 to win the 1996 Masters from 6 back are the myth that 6 back with 18 left is dead, not alive.

myths.reality: Four majors 156 players over 72 holes each — Masters, PGA, US Open, The Open — plus the regular Tour's 40 events that fund them.
Lowest over 72 holes — 4 rounds, cut after 36 to top 65 and ties, so two bad holes on Friday can still miss the weekend even with a Thursday 65.

explainers.question: How do Formula 1 tyres work?
explainers.answer: F1 tyres are 5 dry compounds C1 hard to C5 soft plus intermediate and wet, with 2 dry mandatory per Grand Prix, pit window 1-2 stops, degradation 0.1s per lap vs 0.5s cliff, and the undercut vs overcut that 1 second pit vs 23s pit lane decides.
explain: F1 tyres are 18-inch Pirelli — 5 dry C1 hard (white) to C5 soft (red) plus C2-4 yellow, plus intermediate green and wet blue — each GP picks 3 dry of the 5: e.g. Bahrain C1-C2-C3, Monaco C3-C4-C5 — the 3 per GP plus 8 sets dry per weekend (soft 3 sets, medium 2, hard 1, plus sprint 2 extra?) — the tyre life is 25 laps soft, 35 medium, 45 hard on 2024's abrasiveness, so the degradation cliff at lap 12 for soft's 0.5s per lap after cliff vs 0.1s linear before decides the pit lap, not the fuel, which is why soft starter pits lap 18 while hard starter lap 30.

The 2-dry rule decides strategy. The Grand Prix must use 2 of the 3 dry compounds, so a soft start must finish medium or hard plus mandatory 1 pit — the 1 pit 23 seconds pit lane vs 0.1s per lap degradation makes the undercut vs overcut: pit lap 16 to undercut the leader's pit 17 with fresh medium 1 sec per lap faster — the undercut's 2s gap closes, which is why Verstappen at Monaco pits 16 from soft to hard to undercut Leclerc's 18, not stay out for overcut 20 with clear air but 0.5s degradation cliff.

The evergreen myth is soft always fastest. Soft is 0.8s per lap faster lap 1-5 but degrades 0.5s after cliff lap 12 vs medium's 0.2s after lap 25, so soft at lap 20 is slower than medium new — the soft's 25-lap life vs medium's 35 shows the crossover lap 18 where medium new beats soft old by 1.2s, which is why the 2-stop soft-medium-soft vs 1-stop medium-hard decides Monaco's 1-pit not 2 as tyre choice's crossover.

The pit lane 23 seconds plus stationary 2.1s vs 3.5s slow shows stop's window — the 23s at 60 km/h pit lane vs 350 km/h straight's gap 23s pit lane loses 23s plus 2.1s stop =25s total, so the undercut needs 0.8s per lap x 3 laps =2.4s to recover, which is why undercut lap 16 with 3-lap fresh delta recovers 2.4s vs leader's old soft degradation, not the 0.5 cliff alone — the 23s is the evergreen that makes 2-stop not 1 if tyre degradation's 0.5s after cliff times 10 laps =5s vs pit 25s, so 2-stop loses 50s vs 1-stop 25s but gains 1.5s per lap x 20 =30s, net 20s loss.

The sprint's one-tyre myth vs GP's 2. Sprint 100km uses one tyre no mandatory, GP 305km uses 2 mandatory, so sprint's soft 15 laps 30 minutes with no pit wins 0.5s per lap vs GP's soft-medium must 2 compounds — the 100km sprint's one tyre shows why sprint at Interlagos 24 laps soft only works but GP 71 laps not — soft life 25 not 71, so GP needs medium-hard 45.

explainers.question: How does an F1 pit stop work?
explainers.answer: An F1 pit stop is 2.0 seconds stationary plus 23 seconds pit lane — 3 gunners per wheel plus jack plus stabiliser 22 crew, wheel nuts single hex 400Nm, pit limiter 80 km/h, with 1-2 mandatory stops for 2 dry compounds, not 0 as sprint's one-tyre 100km, and the 2.0 vs 3.5 decides undercut vs overcut.

Pit lane speed 60 Monaco vs 80 elsewhere plus 23s at 60 vs 18s at 80 decides cheap SC 10s vs green 25 — pit lane open under SC/VSC vs closed if incident — the pit limiter 80 electronic vs pit 60 at Monaco with 23s vs 18s, so Monaco 18s not 23, which is why Monaco pit 18s total 20s vs Bahrain 23+2.1=25s 5s faster — the 1-pit Monaco 1st wins with 18s not 25, so Monaco's 1-pit strategy wins with 18s vs 2-pit 36s not 50s, which is why Monaco overtakes 0 + pit 18 decides race, not DRS's 15 mph with no zone as Monaco.

The 2-dry mandatory 1-2 stops decides — mandatory 2 compounds means 1 pit minimum with soft-medium, 2-pit medium-hard-soft for degradation 0.5s cliff at 12 — the pit window lap 16-30 decides undercut with 1 pit vs 2 pits — the sprint 100km uses one tyre no pit, GP 305km uses 1-2 pits for 2 compounds, so sprint's soft 15 laps 100km with no pit wins 0.5s per lap vs 2 compounds — the 2-dry rule's 1 pit minimum with soft-medium, 2-pit 2 stops 50s vs 1-pit 25s, but fresh tyre 1.5s per lap x 20 =30s net faster, which is why 2023 Bahrain Verstappen soft 18 hard 39 1-pit vs others 2-pit soft-medium-hard 2 pits 50s but gain 30s net loss 20s, so 1-pit wins at Bahrain with degradation 0.1 linear before cliff not 0.5 after.

explainers.question: What are constructors vs drivers championships in F1?
explainers.answer: Drivers' is one driver's sum of 25-1 points over 24 GPs, constructors' is team's sum of both drivers' points over 24, with $1bn prize split 14-10% to top team, not the drivers' trophy, with Red Bull's 1st+2nd 25+18=43 per GP vs Williams 11th 1 point, so constructor shows car 70% not driver 30%.
explain: Constructors vs drivers: drivers' championship is driver's 24-race sum 25-1 to 10th plus fastest if top10 — Verstappen's 575 2023 with 19 wins vs Pérez 285 was drivers' 1 vs 2, constructors' is team's sum Verstappen 575 plus Pérez 285 =860 for Red Bull 1st vs Mercedes 2nd 409 (Hamilton 234+Russell 175) =860 vs 409, so Red Bull's constructors 860 not Verstappen alone 575 shows team 70% car plus 2-driver sum vs driver 30% individual — the constructors' 860 prize 14% $140m vs Williams 10th 28 points $15m with cost cap 135m shows car, not pay driver, wins constructors not drivers.

The prize split myth: drivers' trophy is Drivers' (Fangio) trophy with driver's name, constructors' Cup with team trophy $1bn split Pro Rata 14% for 1st (140m), 10% 2nd, 7% 3rd... not equal — the 14% not 5% shows team's $140m vs 9th's $35m with wind-tunnel handicap last 115% vs first 70% aero hours, not equal car, which is why Williams 10th with 28 points prize 35m plus merch 10 not 140 still needs $135m cap gap with owner subsidy vs Red Bull's 860 prize sufficient.

The grid's evergreen myth is drivers equal cars. Drivers not equal as car decides 70% pace — Red Bull's 1-2 43 per GP vs Haas 0 shows car not driver, which is why Pérez 2nd in same car vs Hamilton 3rd in Mercedes 2nd — the same car 1 vs 2 gap 290 points Verstappen-Pérez 290 not 0 shows driver 30% within team, but between teams car's 70% decides 860 vs 409 gap, not Hamilton's 234 beating Pérez's 285? Hamilton 3rd but Mercedes 2nd with Russell sum 409 shows team sum not driver best.
explainers.example: 2023: Verstappen 575 drivers' 1, Pérez 285 2, Hamilton 234 3 — Red Bull constructors 860 (575+285), Mercedes 409 (234+175), Ferrari 406 — constructors 860 prize $140m 14% vs Williams 28 10th $35m — constructors is team's 2-driver sum over 24, drivers' one sum, with 70% car vs 30% driver, wind tunnel last 115% vs first 70% not prize alone.

myths.reality: Constructors is team's 2-driver sum over 24 — Red Bull 860 (575+285) vs Mercedes 409, drivers' 575 vs 285 separate.
Prize 14% for 1st 140m vs 10% 2nd vs 2.5% 10th 25m — Red Bull 140m vs Williams 15m shows 70% car gap.

myths.belief: Best driver in best car always.
myths.reality: Pérez 2nd in best car gap 290 to Verstappen same car shows driver 30% within team, car 70% between teams.

Car decides 70% pace — Red Bull 1-2 43 per GP vs Haas 0 shows car, not just driver 30% gap within team.

explainers.question: What is Formula 1 — and how does it work?
explainers.answer: Formula 1 is 20 drivers in 10 teams in single-seaters at 220 mph over 24 Grands Prix per season from Bahrain in March to Abu Dhabi in December, with points 25-18-15-12-10-8-6-4-2-1 to 10th per race, the constructors' sum of both drivers, and DRS and budget cap as the modern bottlenecks.
explain: Formula 1 is 10 teams of 2 drivers — Red Bull, Mercedes, Ferrari, McLaren, Aston Martin, Alpine, Williams, RB, Sauber, Haas — each builds a 798kg hybrid single-seater with a 1.6L V6 turbo plus 120kW hybrid, at 220 mph on the straight, 5g in corners, with 18-inch Pirelli tyres in 5 compounds from soft to hard and intermediate and wet for rain, so the car, not just the driver, decides about 70% of pace by data.

Weekend explains the evergreen. Three practices Friday-Saturday, qualifying Saturday over Q1, Q2, Q3 knockout — 20, then 15, then 10 — with the fastest lap on soft taking pole, then the Grand Prix Sunday over 190 miles or 2 hours, 44-78 laps by track, with a formation lap, a standing start with 5 lights, and a pit window where the 2-second tyre change can undercut — the 24 weekends are the 24 tracks, from Monaco's 2-mile street to Spa's 4.3-mile mountain.

Points are 25 to 10th. Winner 25, 2nd 18, 3rd 15, 4th 12, 5th 10, 6th 8, 7th 6, 8th 4, 9th 2, 10th 1 plus fastest lap 1 if top 10, so a 1-2 team takes 43 and the 10th takes 1, and the constructors' championship is the sum of both drivers — Red Bull's 1st and 2nd in 2023 was 43 every Sunday, which is why the team title often follows the drivers' title.

DRS explains the overtake. The Drag Reduction System opens the rear wing on a straight if within 1 second of the car ahead at the detection point, adding about 15 mph and 20m of closing — the DRS zone is 600-800m, so the following car gains, not the leader, which is why the lead car defends by braking early to be within 1 second for the next DRS, and why Monaco has no DRS pass while Monza has 3 DRS zones.

The budget cap is the evergreen since 2021. Teams are capped at $135m per season for car development, not driver salaries, so wind-tunnel time is also capped by championship position — last gets 15% more wind tunnel than first — which is why the 10th in December gets more aero hours next year, not more money, and why the 2021-22 caps decided the 2023 pecking order more than the drivers did.
explainers.example: Monza: 53 laps, 190 miles, Verstappen pole at 1:20.1 on soft, race Sunday with one stop soft to hard at lap 20, DRS on the 800m main straight adds 15 mph, Verstappen leads into Turn 1, Leclerc within 1 second gets DRS and closes 20m but cannot pass without over-cut, Red Bull 1-2 takes 43 points, Williams' 10th takes 1 — 24 Grands Prix, 25-1 points, DRS and cap decide more than the 220 mph top speed.

myths.reality: Car is about 70%, driver 30% — qualifying, DRS, strategy and the 2-second pit undercut decide the Sunday more than top speed.

explainers.question: How does rugby union actually work?
explainers.answer: Rugby union is 15-a-side, 80 minutes (2x40), where you carry not dribble, must pass backwards, tackle to the ground, and score 5 points for a try in the in-goal, 2 for the conversion kick, 3 for a penalty kick and 3 for a drop goal — the scrum and lineout are the set pieces that have no football equivalent.
explain: The backward pass explains the shape. Rugby is carried, not dribbled, and the ball must be passed backwards or flat, never forward — a forward pass is a scrum to the other team — so the team moves forward by running through the gain line, not by passing forward, which is why the 10-12-13 centres run the crash and the 9-10 pivot pass back to the wing.

The tackle explains the contest. A tackle brings the ball carrier to ground, the carrier must release, and both sides compete for the ball over it — the ruck — where the tackler must roll away and the arriving players must stay on their feet and enter through the gate behind the hindmost foot, so the breakdown is a second contest after the tackle, not a foul, and clean ball from the ruck lets the scrum-half pass.

The scrum is the restart for minor infringements. Eight forwards per side bind — 3 front row of loosehead, hooker, tighthead, 2 locks, 2 flankers, 1 number 8 — and the scrum-half feeds the ball mid-tunnel, the hooker hooks, and the pack pushes on the referee's crouch-bind-set, with penalties for early push or wheeling — the scrum is a shoving contest that can win a penalty 30 metres out, which is why South Africa pick 6 locks on the bench as the Bomb Squad.

The lineout is the throw. When the ball goes out, the hooker throws 5-15m between two lines of jumpers lifted by teammates, with the jumper who catches forming a maul — a driving bind — that can march 20m, so the lineout is the platform for the rolling maul try that looks illegal but is legal if the ball stays at the back and the maul does not collapse.

Scoring is 5+2+3+3. A try is 5 for grounding the ball in the 10-22m in-goal, conversion is 2 from the spot in line with the try 20m out, penalty 3 through the H posts, drop goal 3 on the run — a 5-point try plus 2 makes 7, so a 3-point kick is less than half a try, which is why teams chase tries at 14-12 down late, not kicks, and why the Six Nations table has 4 points for a win plus bonus for 4 tries or losing by 7.

Discipline is cards with teeth. A yellow is 10 minutes in the sin bin with 14 men, a red is 14 men for the rest after the 2023 law — and since 2023 a 20-minute red lets the player be replaced after 20, so the game is 15 vs 15 again but the sent-off player is gone — the 20-minute red is the bottleneck that changed 6 Nations discipline more than any law since.

explainers.question: What is the Rugby Championship?
explainers.answer: The Rugby Championship is the southern 4-nation July-September — New Zealand, South Africa, Australia and Argentina play home-and-away double round-robin 6 games each over 7 weeks, 12 games total, 4 points for win plus try and losing bonuses, not the Six Nations' single round where February cold not July sun decides.
explain: The Rugby Championship is 4 nations 6 games each — each plays the other 3 twice, home and away, 2 vs NZ at Eden Park, 2 vs SA at Ellis Park, 2 vs ARG at Vélez — 12 games total over 7 weeks with one bye per team — the Championship's 6 per team vs Six Nations' 5 per team is one more game, but the Championship's 2x home-and-away vs Six Nations' single 2H-3A alternate yearly — the 2x means the Ellis Park altitude 1,750m's advantage repeats for SA not just alternate, which is why NZ's Eden Park 30-year unbeaten home vs Six Nations' Twickenham 82k alternate matters differently.

Points as Six Nations: 4 for win plus bonus for 4 tries or losing by 7, so 6-game max 30 plus? Actually 6 wins =24 plus 6 try bonuses maybe 30, not 23 as Six Nations' 5-0 Slam bonus 3 — the Championship's 6-0 not 5-0 has no Slam bonus 3, so the 6-0 max is 24 plus 6 =30 with no extra, which is why NZ's 6-0 2023 with 5 try bonuses 29 beats SA 4-2 with 2 bonuses 18 by 11 not 3 as Slam would.

The evergreen is Argentina 2012. Argentina joined 2012 as 4th after Tri Nations 1996-2011 with 3 — the 4th made 6 from 4, not 4 from 3 — the Pumas' 2022 win over NZ at Christchurch and 2023 over Australia at Parra shows the 4th not dead weight — Wales' Six Nations Wooden Spoon 2023 with no wins vs Argentina's 2-4 still competitive, which is why the Championship's 4 closed not 6 as Six Nations with Italy, so Arg never Spoon but can be 4th with 0-6.

The myth is closed 4 forever. The Championship's closed 4 vs Six Nations' fixed 6 — no promotion as Europe's Rugby Championship plus Georgia vs 2023 6-0 Portugal repechage not — the Championship's 4 plus Japan invite talk for 5 has no promotion, like EuroLeague's 18 licences not open qualifier, so the Championship's 12 games vs Six Nations' 15 with similar TV dollars shows the 4's double round has 12 vs 15 with not open promotion.

The July-September sun vs February rain explains style. The Championship's July winter in NZ/SA is 10°C dry with hard pitches vs Six Nations February 5°C wet heavy — the hard not heavy favours running rugby with 6 tries per game vs forward wet with 3, which is why the final's 6-game double round's running shows where Six Nations' 5-game forward shows the autumn internations November cross-hemisphere to decide world 1, not just the hemisphere's table.

explainers.question: What is the Six Nations?
explainers.answer: The Six Nations is rugby union's 6-team, 5-round league each February-March — England, France, Ireland, Wales, Scotland and Italy play each other once, 2 home 3 away alternating yearly, 4 points for a win, bonus for 4 tries or losing by 7, with the Grand Slam for 5 wins and the Wooden Spoon for 0.
explain: The Six Nations is 6 teams in a single round-robin — 5 games per nation over 7 weeks in February-March, with one bye week and one fallow week, so the championship has 15 games total, each 80 minutes, with no semi or final — the table after 5 decides, which is why the last Saturday has three games at 14:15, 16:45 and 20:00 to stagger the deciders, like football's last day but with 5, not 38.

Points are 4 for a win, 2 for a draw, 1 bonus for 4 tries, 1 bonus for losing by 7 or less — so a team can get 2 points from a loss with 4 tries and a close margin, and a 5-0 Grand Slam winner gets a 3-point bonus for the Slam, so 5 wins is 20 plus 3 = 23 max, while a 4-1 without bonuses is 16 — the bonus makes a 4-try win more valuable than a 3-try win even with the same 4 points for the win.

The venues alternate yearly. England at 82,000 Twickenham with 82,000 for France, France at 80,000 Stade de France, Ireland at 51,700 Aviva, Wales at 73,000 Principality, Scotland at 67,000 Murrayfield, Italy at 68,000 Olimpico — the 2-home-3-away flip each year decides the title as much as form, because a year with England away at France and Ireland is harder than the home year.

Why the Six Nations is not the Rugby Championship is the hemisphere. The Rugby Championship is 4 teams — New Zealand, South Africa, Australia, Argentina — in July-September with 2x home-and-away, so the Six Nations' February cold and rain produces forward-led low-scoring games, while the Championship's July sun produces running rugby — the same sport in opposite seasons, which is why the Six Nations winner and the Rugby Championship winner meet in the autumn internationals to decide the world number one.

The Wooden Spoon is the evergreen myth. No trophy, but the last-placed team is said to hold the Spoon — Italy have 18 since joining in 2000, Wales have 12, England 12 historically — and the Spoon in 2023 was Italy who beat Wales in Cardiff to avoid it, so the bottom game in round 5 can be as charged as the top, because the Spoon, like relegation, is the anti-title that still fills the stadium.
explainers.example: Last Saturday 2023: Ireland need a win at home vs England to win the Slam — 4 points plus 3-point Slam bonus, France need a bonus-point win and an Ireland loss to overtake, Wales vs Italy is Spoon decider in Rome — Ireland win 29-10 with 4 tries for the Slam and 13-point bonus, France win with bonus but stay on 19, so the Slam bonus decides the table by 3, not points difference alone.

myths.reality: Single round-robin 5 games per nation over 7 weeks, 4 points for a win plus try and losing bonuses, Grand Slam bonus for 5 wins, no semi or final.
4 tries gets 1 bonus win or lose, losing by 7 gets 1 — a 4-try loss beats a 3-try win on bonuses, which is why teams chase the 4th try at 30-10 even when the win is gone.

myths.belief: It is always the same venues.
myths.reality: 2 home 3 away alternating yearly — a year with France and Ireland away is harder than the home year, which decides many titles.
